subject: Top-up order: prepaid capacity escrow option + signoff checklist
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@orbitcloud.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:34 -0800
Subject: Proposed top-up + escrow payment option

Hi Logan / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — OrbitCloud is ready to move forward with an initial top-up purchase of 250k inference units to cover our Q4 burst needs. Finance asked whether Redwood can accept the prepayment into escrow (third-party escrow agent) with release triggers tied to monthly consumption thresholds and service availability SLA milestones. They want the money held until redwood confirms delivery metrics for the first two months.

Attached is our PO (OrbitCloud_PO_20261102.pdf). We prefer the escrow approach to avoid reclassifying the funds as prepaid revenue on our books until the work is validated. Please advise whether Redwood supports escrow, and if so what the standard escrow release language would look like. If escrow isn't possible, what are the alternative accounting-friendly structures?

Next steps: can we get a short change-order draft and a list of the minimal legal / procurement items your team would need to sign?

Thanks,
Sasha Patel
Senior Procurement Manager | OrbitCloud
procurement@orbitcloud.com

Attachments: OrbitCloud_PO_20261102.pdf (pdf, 78KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@orbitcloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:04:09 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed top-up + escrow payment option

Hi Sasha — appreciate the clear PO. Redwood can accommodate a couple of approaches depending on OrbitCloud's accounting preference:

1) Standard change order (prepaid credits on Redwood books) with 12-month expiration and monthly consumption reporting;
2) Third-party escrow: Redwood signs the change order that references an escrow agreement and release triggers; escrow agent releases funds monthly as consumption is validated; we typically require an escrow agent with documented release mechanics;
3) Conditional credit hold: funds are held in Redwood's merchant account but subject to a simple consumption-based refund clause for the first 60 days.

I've attached a short change-order template (COA_topup_proposal_20261103.pdf) that implements option 2 language as a draft — includes escrow placeholders. Please note that option 2 requires legal approval and an escrow agent name.

Jonas / Laura — looping you in to confirm if the escrow language in the attached draft is acceptable from legal/finance. Quick ask: can we get redline suggestions by Thursday so we can share a countersigned change order and a DocuSign link to OrbitCloud?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai

Attachments: COA_topup_proposal_20261103.pdf (draft change order, 42KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 14:16:51 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed top-up + escrow payment option

Logan — thanks for the draft. I reviewed the escrow clauses and added a focused redline for Section 7 (payment & release mechanics). High level: we are open to using a third-party escrow agent, but we must ensure the following controls are in the change order or linked escrow agreement:

- Clear, objective release triggers tied to throttled usage logs (we will provide monthly consumption reports)
- A defined dispute-resolution path before escrow release delays lead to service interruption (we propose a 15-day cure window)
- Escrow agent must be neutral and approved by both parties in writing
- A cap on refunds for failed delivery that aligns with our liability limits in the MSA (no unlimited refund obligations)

I attached the redlined excerpt for Section 7 (MSA_section7_redline_20261104.docx). Please note one legal checkbox: OrbitCloud's draft language asked for immediate escrow release on "service availability confirmation" — we need to avoid any release trigger tied to subjective terms. Replace with quantitative SLA measurements (e.g., 99.5% monthly availability measured by our monitoring and cross-checked against your logs).

Next steps I propose:
- Logan to share the redline to OrbitCloud as annotated change order and tag the escrow agent field as TBD;
- Laura to confirm finance treatment (prepaid vs escrow) and whether Redwood can accept funds into a dedicated merchant subaccount pending escrow execution;
- Karthik to prepare internal playbook for DocuSign + procurement checklist so sales ops can close quickly.

If we get confirmation on the agent and SLA metrics by Friday EOD, legal can sign off early next week.

— Jonas
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: MSA_section7_redline_20261104.docx (redline, 18KB)

Hi Sasha — following up with Redwood's procurement checklist and our preferred small edits. We've reviewed the PO and Logan's draft change order. Finance can accept escrow in principle but needs either: (A) escrow agent + agreement, or (B) payment to a dedicated merchant subaccount that Redwood holds subject to the change-order refund mechanics.

Minimal items needed to close: 
- Counter-signed change order (COA_topup_proposal_20261103.pdf) that incorporates Jonas's redline on objective SLA release triggers
- Escrow agent name or confirmation to use Option B (dedicated merchant subaccount)
- PO referencing the Redwood change order ID and the deal id (OC-2026-11-09)
- Confirmation of credit expiration window — OrbitCloud requested 12 months; finance prefers 18 months for this commercial structure. Please confirm acceptable term.

If OrbitCloud is okay with 18 months for credit expiration, we can route the change order to DocuSign today and have Karthik run the sign-off checklist in parallel. Otherwise, we'll need a short approval from Finance Head.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
